blocks.text: Sometime this month, the first of the migratory birds will come down over Candaba. They have been doing it for longer than anyone has kept records: ducks, herons and shorebirds flying in from northern Asia to spend the dry months on the wetlands of Pampanga. They come because, for a few months every year, Candaba is water. We tend to forget that. On the map, Candaba is a town, a stretch of rice land, a viaduct that motorists cross without looking down.
